Author: CrownedPandaXIV
Name: XIV Fleet Companion
Description:
Got a massive fleet of submarines? Always struggling to see which ones need upgrades? Wanna see your multi-account fleet at a glance? Give this a try!

This plugin sends your fleet to the free XIV Fleet Companion app for Windows, which shows it all in one window. Get the app from https://github.com/CrownedPandaXIV/XIVFleetCompanion-Releases

Needs:
• AutoRetainer (from https://love.puni.sh/ment.json)

Works best with:
• Allagan Tools: bags, retainers' items and FC chests
• FC Tracker (from https://puni.sh/api/repository/erdelf): FC houses
• Submarine Tracker: voyage loot

Thanks to kawaii, NightmareXIV and the Puni.sh team (AutoRetainer), Critical_Impact (Allagan Tools), erdelf (FC Tracker) and Infi (Submarine Tracker) for their plugins.
Punchline: Here to help manage your EMPIAH!
Changelog:
The fleet inside the game: every page of the app in the plugin's own window (Summary, Subs, Route Optimization, Parts, Supplies, Salvage, Roster, Retainers, Free Companies, Inventory, Income, Gil & Market, Trends, PCs), the app's edits made from the game, and Fleet in the game's info bar. Needs app 1.8.0, which adds what the plugin reads to the database: open the app once after updating. Built in stages, each tried as a test build first:

- Stage 1: speed test. Main window → Speed test (2.0) (or /xivfleet speedtest) times reading from the database what the in-game Summary, Subs and Supplies windows will need: connecting, characters, subs, retainers, ceruleum and repair kits in FC chests, their use over the last 14 days, and the PCs. Three rounds, with the first, best and worst time of each, and the longest game frame meanwhile to show it doesn't stutter. It runs in the background, only reads, and Copy results copies it all to share.
- Stage 2: the database views. The speed test also times reading the ready-made views app 1.8.0 adds to the database (subs, supplies and the summary), which work things out in the database instead of in the plugin. With an older app they show as failed.
- Stage 3: one main window with tabs. /xivfleet (or the plugin's button in Dalamud) opens one window with Summary, Subs, Supplies, Status and Settings tabs; /xivfleet subs (or summary, supplies, status, settings) opens it at that tab, and Dalamud's settings button opens the Settings tab. Look only for now.
- Summary: subs back and waiting, out (and when the next is back) and in port; ventures done and retainers without one; characters below the low-supply warnings and the first to run out.
- Subs: every built sub with its character, rank, build and a live countdown, grouped by character, with a filter.
- Supplies: each character's ceruleum and repair kits, use per day, days left (amber under a week, red under three days) and how many to buy, as in the app.
- Status is the old main window (connections, Check what I can see, the speed test); Settings the old settings window.
- Click a column's header in Subs or Supplies to sort by it, again to reverse it (Status: soonest back first; rows with nothing to sort by, like a sub in port or a character without enough history, go last). Drag a column's edge to make it wider; the columns still stretch with the window, and the game remembers the widths.
- The numbers come from the app's views in the database (app 1.8.0 or later), read in the background while the window is open: subs every 30 seconds, supplies and the summary every 5 minutes, or on Refresh.
- Stage 4: what needs attention, and Fleet in the info bar.
- The Summary starts with Needs attention: subs back and waiting, then Free Company houses not entered for a while (red from 30 days), characters low on ceruleum or repair kits, characters no longer synced, and setups where AutoRetainer wasn't running. The same rules as the app's Summary. No pop-ups and nothing in chat.
- "Fleet" in the game's info bar (top right, by the clock), always there so the window is one click away; "Fleet: 4 back · 1 low · 2 to check" when something needs you. Hover for the list, click to open the Summary. On by default; Settings → "Show Fleet in the game's info bar" turns it off. While it's shown it reads the subs and what needs attention every 30 seconds (a few milliseconds each), never the heavier supplies.
- Stage 5: the sidebar, the looks and the new icon.
- The tabs make way for a sidebar: the submarine at the top, then the pages in three groups that fold (Fleet: Summary, Subs, Supplies; Tools: Check what I can see, Speed test; System: Status, Settings), each with an icon and, beside it, what needs attention (Subs · 4 back, Supplies · 1 low, Summary · how many things). The button at the top folds it down to its icons (hover one for its name and count). At its foot, when this PC last synced, or why it isn't syncing.
- Check what I can see and the speed test are pages of the window now, not windows of their own; the credits are on the Status page.
- Looks (Settings → Look): XIV Fleet Companion (the app's colors, the new default), Dalamud (like other plugins) or High contrast; and colour-blind friendly status colors (blue, yellow and orange-red in place of green, amber and red). Only this window changes.
- The new submarine icon, for the plugin's picture and its icon in Dalamud's plugin list.
- Stage 6: the rest of the tabs, part 1: Roster, Retainers and PCs. Three more pages, sorted and filtered like Subs, read every minute while shown (app 1.8.0's views, from its test.8):
- Roster (Fleet): every character with its Free Company, house, gil, ceruleum and repair kits (red below the low-supply warnings), retainers and subs, when it last synced and which setup syncs it; "not synced" beside one the plugin no longer syncs. The sidebar says how many aren't synced.
- Retainers (Fleet): every retainer with its owner, class and level, gil, average item level, venture and a live countdown (Venture Complete in green, Idle in amber), and its gear target. The sidebar says how many ventures are done.
- PCs (System): every setup of the plugin with its version (amber when older than another PC's), last sync, characters, which plugins it found and what it couldn't see (hover); then each setup's last "Check what I can see". The sidebar counts setups where AutoRetainer wasn't running.
- Class, venture and item names and item levels come from the game's own files, so they're right on patch day.
- These pages only show for now: reordering or removing characters, setting retainers' gear targets and removing a PC stay in the app.
- /xivfleet roster, /xivfleet retainers and /xivfleet pcs open them.
- Stage 6, part 2: Free Companies and Inventory, and the app's table controls everywhere.
- Free Companies (Fleet): every Free Company with its leader, world, points, members, house (or, without one, when it can bid) and how long since a member entered it (amber from the house warning, red from 30 days or with no date). The sidebar counts houses not entered for a while.
- Inventory (Fleet), as the app's: Characters (what chosen characters and their retainers hold), Free Companies (chosen FC chests), Fleet totals (each item across the fleet, the most first) and Where is it? (type part of an item's name: every place the fleet holds it, in the Roster's order, by account). HQ items say so.
- Every table (Subs, Supplies, Roster, Retainers, Free Companies, PCs, Inventory) works like the app's: click a heading to sort, again for the other way, a third time to go back; Reset Sort goes back at once; Columns shows, hides and reorders the columns (remembered; Reset columns undoes it); Group by account while not sorted. Long tables only draw the rows on screen.
- Retainers in the app's order: by their owner's place in the Roster, then hiring order. The Roster and the Free Companies follow the Roster's saved order too.
- The Summary's retainer line matches the app's and updates every 30 seconds instead of every 5 minutes, so a retainer caught between two ventures while AutoRetainer sends it out again no longer shows "without a venture" for minutes. Retainers of characters no longer synced are left out, as in the app.
- /xivfleet fcs and /xivfleet inventory open the new pages.
- Fleet in the info bar keeps working after an update. Right after the plugin updated, clicking "Fleet" could do nothing until the plugin was turned off and on: the old copy's entry was still on screen. The plugin now asks again every few seconds until "Fleet" is its own, and takes it back if it ever isn't (noted in /xllog).
- Stage 6, part 3: Salvage and Income (with app 1.8.0's views). Salvage: the salvage each character holds, standard and extravagant, with each piece on hover and its value at the fixed salvage prices. Income: each character's real net income per day from its subs (salvage that came in, less repair kits used) and the venture rewards per character at what a vendor pays (from the game's files), over the Income window set in the app. Read every 5 minutes while shown. Fight Club's expected figures and Loot per Voyage come later in 2.x, with routes. /xivfleet salvage and /xivfleet income open them. Salvage leads with the Fleet-Wide Salvage Total, each hover ends with its total (pieces and gil), and the Summary shows the Fleet-Wide Salvage Total too, as the app's. The Summary also shows the venture income per day (last days of the Income window, at what a vendor pays), read with the supplies.
- Tables that read at a glance: colours that mean something (green when fine, amber getting low, red well below a warning: the Roster's ceruleum and repair kits against the app's warnings, Supplies' days left, Last synced, Income, houses, the PCs' plugins), subs as dots out of the slots unlocked, numbers on the right, large gil as "5.86M" (the full amount on hover), the world softer after each name, a band for each account with how many it has (and, on the Roster, which setup syncs it, so Synced by is hidden by default; Columns brings it back), a little more room per row and stronger stripes.
- Gil in gold, house addresses in blue and Free Company names in lavender (Roster, Retainers, Free Companies, Salvage). The warning colour is now orange rather than gold, so it's never mistaken for gil. With colour blind status colours these three stay plain, so the only colours there are the ones that mean something. The app uses the same colours.
- Every column can be resized, the last one too: columns keep the width they're given (fitted to their contents at first) instead of all stretching to fill the window, so the room left over sits after the last column, and a table wider than the window scrolls sideways. Column widths saved before this start over once.
- Livelier Subs and Retainers. Subs: each character is named once over its subs (while the table isn't sorted by a column), a thin bar beside the rank shows how far to the next, and the dashes in builds are softer. Retainers: each owner is named once, the class is in its role's colour (tanks blue, healers green, damage red, a base class such as Gladiator or Conjurer a lighter shade; gatherers plain) with the level softer, Avg ilvl is green when the gear meets the retainer's gear target and amber when it falls short (checked as the app does, from the game's files), and a venture's countdown is followed by the time it's done.
- FC points in aqua; ceruleum and repair kits that don't count toward the warnings (no sub built, or not synced) dim rather than plain; Income's tables name each character with its world, as everywhere else; and salvage totals (the Salvage page and the Summary) in gil's gold.
- Stage 6 part 4: Parts, as the app's Parts tab. Detail: every part a sub needs for the build it should have at its rank (its Sub Rules, or Fight Club's best build after repair kits for a sub ticked Craft? from rank 85), a new workshop's first sub and every unlocked empty slot, and where each comes from: a spare in bags, a retainer or the FC chest (a shared chest never promises one part twice), the part another sub gives up when upgraded, or crafting. To craft: how many of each part. The Summary shows the parts to craft and the subs ready for new parts with what each needs; the sidebar, the Summary's count and the info bar ("2 need parts") count them too. Worked out in the plugin from the app's views, the same way as the app (its tests write made-up fleets and the app's answers, which the plugin's tests check against). Sub Rules and Craft? are set in the app; Look ahead comes later in 2.x.
- New subs to build count as ready for parts too: a sub not built yet in an open slot is counted and listed with the subs ready for new parts ("7 subs are ready for new parts, 1 new sub to build") on the Summary, the Parts page, the sidebar and the info bar, with its four parts on the Summary.
- Stage 7: market prices. A Gil & Market page, as the app's tab: the fleet's gil (characters and retainers) and gil per account, what's up for sale, and the listings unsold for a while (the app's days setting), oldest first. With Live Market Prices on in the app's Settings, the plugin asks Universalis itself (only item numbers and world, data center and region names are sent; answers kept 30 minutes): each listing's cheapest rival on its world, data center and region, the undercut listings (someone sells cheaper on the same world; biggest gap first, and a count beside the page in the sidebar), and venture rewards at market prices on the Income page and the Summary. With it off, nothing is asked. The Summary shows the listings unsold for a while, as the app's tile. The app's tests run its own Universalis code on canned listings, and the plugin's tests check it gets the same answers.
- Live prices no longer hold up the rest. The prices are asked of Universalis in the background, apart from the database reads, so the Summary, Supplies, Salvage and every other page keep updating while they come in (the Gil & Market page says "Getting live prices from Universalis..." meanwhile). Each world, data center and region is asked once, only for the items listed or earned on its worlds, up to 4 requests at a time instead of one after another.
- No more slowdown with live prices on. The window worked out every listing's rivals and every venture reward at market prices again on each frame, which took most of a second and dropped the game to about 1 FPS. It's now worked out once per read, in the background, and kept (a test times it: about 2 microseconds a frame after).
- Stage 8: routes. As the app's Subs tab, worked out by the plugin itself (from the new fleet_route_* views and the game's own sea map data):
- The Subs page gains Next Rank (when it ranks up, "≈" when worked out from game data alone, how on hover), Next Build (its next build from the Sub Rules or Fight Club, green when it can switch now), Current Route (with the map's number), Current Gil/Day and Target Gil/Day in gold, and Target Route (green when it's on it, amber when it isn't). Speed and Range can be added with Columns.
- A Route Optimization page: subs from rank 85 not on Fight Club's best route for their rank, biggest gain first, with a count beside it in the sidebar and a line on the Summary.
- Income gains Fight Club's Expected / day and Of expected (amber under 90%, red under 75%), and the fleet's total against expected.
- Look ahead on the Parts page (3, 7 or 14 days): the parts of each sub's next build due by then, after what's needed now, with when each is due. The app's tests write made-up fleets and the app's answers, and the plugin's tests check every sub's route, gil a day, dates, next build and Look ahead come out the same.
- Loot per Voyage on the Income page, as the app's: what each voyage really brought back over the Income window, from Submarine Tracker, per sub (with its route, voyages, gil a voyage and a day, and Fight Club's expected) and per route; with live prices, at the market on the sub's world, data center and region too (worked out in the background).
- Next Rank forecasts on the Subs page: how close the dates the app saved came to the real rank-ups, each recent one on hover. Both are checked against the app's answers for the same made-up fleets.
- Shopping List on the Parts page, as the app's: the sub parts to craft (Look ahead's too), everything to craft on the way in the order to make it, and the raw materials and crystals to gather or buy, less what the fleet holds in bags, saddlebags, crystals, retainers and Free Company chests (where, on hover). Buy from vendors, Show items already held in full and Copy as Text, as in the app. With Live Market Prices on, each part's cheapest listing against what making it costs (each ingredient on hover), each material's cheapest way, and what buying instead costs, from the world, data center or region chosen in Prices from (asked of Universalis in the background). The recipes come from the game's own files, so it works without the app's game data. Parts ticked off in the app show as made; ticking them off in the game comes later in 2.x. Checked against the app's answers for made-up fleets, recipes and listings, every way of asking. Each of its tables is only as tall as its rows and the page scrolls as a whole, so every section shows. The Parts page now remembers Look ahead, as the app does. Market prices look at the 100 cheapest listings of each item (as the app now does), and "only 1,639 of 2,277 for sale" says plainly what buying those costs and that the rest can't be bought there right now. Craft first's market board prices have the same hover, for the ones still to make, as the app's.
- A PC that only reads follows a moved database. When the app moves the database to another PC, the in-game pages now follow it the same way syncing does, so a PC with syncing off switches by itself (it only needs the old database PC to be on the first time it reads afterwards). While the move is copying, the pages say so and keep what they read before.
- Trends, as the app's Trends tab: any recorded value (gil, ceruleum, repair kits, retainers, subs, sub slots, FC points, salvage value and items) for the whole fleet, or up to 8 characters or Free Companies side by side, over 24 hours to all time. Hover for the values at any time, drag across to zoom in, or show it as a table. Under the chart, each line's value now, its change over the span (and its share), a day on average, and its lowest and highest. Also the Summary's trend tiles for the last 30 days, a chart at the top of the Roster, Salvage and Free Companies pages (folded away until opened, remembered), and each character's or Free Company's own trends from the chart button beside its name. Read in the background with the same chart query as the app, and checked against the app's answers for a made-up history.
- Changing things from the game, as in the app (and saved for the app too): Craft? on the Subs page; Sub Rules on the Parts page (their own tab: rank, slots, each part's class, one character or everyone; add, save, delete with a second click to be sure); gear targets on the Retainers page (Edit beside each target); the Roster order (Change order: up, down, to the top, then save); how many days counts as unsold on Gil & Market; the Income window; removing a PC no longer used (PCs page, with a second click to be sure); and ticking parts off on the Shopping List. Each is saved in the background, then everything is read again; "Saved" or why not shows for a few seconds. Checked against the app's own edits on the same database (the same rows written, the same refusals). Removing a character stays in the app.
- A tidier Summary: Subs, Retainers and Supplies side by side, each with its main figure large; the subs ready for new parts as a table with one part to a line; one "Updated" line at the top (each read on hover).
- The class, then the slot, everywhere ("Shark Hull", "Whale Bridge"), and the Parts tables show Needed before Slot.
- Gil in gil's gold everywhere: headings and notes on Income and Gil & Market, the Summary, and the Gil and Salvage value trends.
- New columns show for someone who chose a table's columns before they were added (Craft? on Subs, Remove on PCs): each table now remembers which columns it had, and one added since shows until it's hidden.
- Free Companies name each FC with its world after it, softer, instead of a separate World column (its members are all on it); a sub's rank sits right after its bar, both on the left, so stretching the column doesn't pull them apart.
- Settings shared with the app, from the game. Settings has a Shared with the app section, saved in the database so the app and every PC use the same: What do you run? (subs, retainers or both; pages and Summary boxes for what you don't run are left out, as in the app), Live Market Prices, the repair kit cost and the Warnings (low repair kits and ceruleum, the FC house warning, when a character counts as not synced). Each is checked the same way as in the app (with app 1.8.0's fleet_settings_view).
- Import Fight Club Data from the game. Settings → Fight Club Data → Import Fight Club Data: choose Fight Club's route spreadsheet (.xlsx), check the rows (rows with a problem start unticked, as in the app), add a patch label if you like, and import. It replaces the stored routes all at once, and leaves them as they were if anything fails. It reads the spreadsheet the same way as the app (merged cells, numbers typed as text, columns moved or missing) and works with the one-file SQLite database too. Old .xls files: save them as .xlsx first.
- A PC that only reads shows on the PCs page. A PC whose plugin syncs no characters (syncing off, or none ticked) now checks in every few minutes while the game runs, so the app's PCs tab and the plugin's PCs page list it ("Only reads"), and moving the database checks it can follow (with app 1.8.0).
- Five new looks, chosen from a dropdown (Settings → Look, with a strip of each look's colours and a line about it on hover): Princess (neon and pastel pink on deep plum, pink headings and a glowing selected page), Deep Sea (navy and teal with glowing cyan), Sunset Harbor (dusky purple with rose-gold), Parchment (a light look: cream with dark brown text and ink blue) and Evergreen (forest green with soft teal), beside XIV Fleet Companion, Dalamud and High contrast. The app has the same looks. Colour-blind friendly status colors work with every look: each has its own shades of blue, yellow and orange-red for fine, a look and urgent, measured to stay readable on its background and apart with every common kind of colour blindness (Parchment uses a raspberry red for urgent, as dark orange and ochre look alike with red-blindness).
- The sidebar in groups: Overview (Summary, Trends), Submarines (Subs, Route Optimization, Parts, Supplies, Salvage), Characters (Roster, Retainers, Free Companies, Inventory) and Gil (Income, Gil & Market), then Tools and System, each group folding away on its own. The app's sidebar has the same groups. With retainers only, Submarines is left out.
- Searching word by word in every Filter box and Where is it?: every word typed, in any order ("diadochos healing" finds every piece of Diadochos healing gear).
- Hide equipped gear on the Inventory page's Characters, Fleet totals and Where is it?: leaves out gear being worn by the characters and their retainers. One choice for all three, saved.
- Free Companies and Inventory read with real Free Company ids. These ids are too big for the number the plugin read them into, so the Free Companies list failed and took every other read down with it ("Could not reach the database" everywhere until the next read, and again on every Refresh). They're read in full now, and a read that fails for any reason other than the connection now fails alone, saying why, keeping what it read before.
- Where is it?'s columns line up. Every item's table now has the same column widths (from the widest text shown), instead of each sizing to its own rows.
